commit.message:
docs(sequentialthinking): state the thought box's limits exactly

The row cap counts thought-text rows only (a long branchId's header rows
are not capped), so there is no absolute size guarantee; and the tool
result never carries the thought text, which the server keeps whole in
its history. README, changeset and the MAX_BOX_ROWS comment now say so.

commit.message:
fix(sequentialthinking): size the thought box after its summary row

A truncated thought of short lines had a summary row wider than the box
(33 characters against a 20-character border). The row texts are now
collected first and the box is sized to include the summary; widening
cannot change the wrapping, since below the cap no line wrapped and at
the cap the summary fits. The very-many-lines test checks every row's
width.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: cliffhall <cliff@futurescale.com>

fix(everything): give gzip-file-as-resource's resource the resource icons

#3131 put a light/dark icon pair on every primitive, and the docs say
every resources/list entry carries one, but the resource the gzip tool
creates had none: the 2025-era session resource (its list entry and
link) and the 2026-07-28 minted link. Both now carry RESOURCE_ICONS, and
the icon tests cover the generated resource in both eras.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: cliffhall <cliff@futurescale.com>

fix(sequentialthinking): bound the stderr thought box

#5205 padded every row of the box to the thought's longest line, so one
long line and many short ones logged their product: a 60 KB thought wrote
400 million characters. The box is now at most MAX_BOX_TEXT_WIDTH (100)
wide, wrapping longer lines and a longer header without splitting a
surrogate pair, and at most MAX_BOX_ROWS (1000) rows, ending with a row
that counts the lines left out. The box tops out near 107 KB; the stored
thought and the tool result are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: cliffhall <cliff@futurescale.com>

commit.message:
fix(filesystem): move minimatch to ^11.0.4 for GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249

Every minimatch 10.x is below the fixed 11.0.1, so the declared ^10.0.1
kept every install on an affected version, and a dependent cannot fix it
for its users because npm reads overrides only from the root project.
The server's one call shape, minimatch(path, pattern, { dot: true }),
is unchanged in 11.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: cliffhall <cliff@futurescale.com>

fix(deps): raise the qs override to >=6.16.1 for GHSA-6pq8-jhm2-2vcw

qs <=6.16.0 throws an uncaught TypeError from stringify with
arrayFormat 'comma' on an element carrying a non-callable own toString.
It reaches everything through express. The fix is inside the range the
root override already pins, so the override's floor moves up and the
lock resolves 6.17.1.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: cliffhall <cliff@futurescale.com>

commit.message:
docs(security-advisory): bring the fix to v2/main through an opaque public PR

The skill and AGENTS.md said an advisory's draft card converts to an issue
only after publication, so the public PR that actually brings the fix to
v2/main had no issue to close and no card to track it. Describe the flow as
it is run: convert the card to an issue that keeps its opaque title when the
fix is ready to merge, push the fork's branch under the same opaque name,
open a public PR that closes that issue with no Copilot loop, merge, close
the fork's PR, and give the issue its public title only after publication.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: cliffhall <cliff@futurescale.com>

fix(scripts): read gh replies over 1 MiB in release:notes and the sweeps

run() in scripts/release-notes.mjs called spawnSync with Node's default
1 MiB maxBuffer, so the src/ tree query at v2.2.0's merge commit
(1,087,532 bytes) aborted the run with ENOBUFS. Pass a 256 MiB
maxBuffer. scripts/lib/sweep.mjs's gh() gets the same: the Dependabot
alert listing is about 7 KB per alert, so ~150 open alerts would
overflow it.

Tests drive the real spawnSync with a >1 MiB reply, and check a genuine
spawn error is still rethrown.

Closes #5339

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: cliffhall <cliff@futurescale.com>

docs(release): document the ledger's title, layout and required sections

Step 4d now titles the page "Servers vX.Y.Z Release Ledger", starts it
from the previous release's ledger (found through the latest Release's
notes, so the skill holds no URL that goes stale), adds the SDKs and
Toolchain masthead lines and the Preparation PRs, tool-schema, LLM
client and advisory-fix sections, names the issue-table columns and
tags, and covers a second merge PR.

Closes #5343

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: cliffhall <cliff@futurescale.com>

docs(release): link the Prepare Python Release PR with addCloseIssueReferences

Step 2c of the release skill now links the workflow-opened PR to the
release issue and reads the link back (the pr-flow step 6 recipe), and
says the by-hand fallback does the same. RELEASING.md says so next to
the Version Packages sentence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: cliffhall <cliff@futurescale.com>

Remove the @claude mention workflow (claude.yml)

The maintainers do not use it, nearly every run it starts is a skip that
clutters the Actions tab and PR checks, and it held ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
Delete the workflow and its trusted-author test, and drop the references
in AGENTS.md (tree entry, Credentialed workflow jobs), verify-action-pins'
header and sdk-watch.yml's secret comment. The historical design record in
docs/agent-guidance-inception.md is left as written.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: cliffhall <cliff@futurescale.com>
